title: LISD Students Take the Courtroom in Webb County Mock Trial
excerpt: Laredo ISD students got a front-row lesson in how the justice system works Wednesday, taking part in a mock trial in a real Webb County courtroom — learning about the rule of law, jury service, and the jobs that keep a courtroom running.
content:
Webb County hosted another mock trial for local students on Wednesday, giving Laredo ISD students a hands-on look at how the justice system works — in a real courtroom.

The mock trial was hosted by Webb County Court at Law No. 2 Judge Victor Villarreal. Students attended the trial of “Cruel Elia v. Pancho Clos,” a fictional case staged to teach them how a trial unfolds.

Along the way, the students learned about the rule of law, the consequences of breaking the law, and the real aspects of jury trials — including the importance of jury service, how a courtroom is laid out, and the occupations within the judiciary.

The lessons were brought to life in the best place to learn them, the county said: in the courtroom itself.

Webb County thanked Judge Villarreal, his staff and the participants for educating the students in a fun way.

Sources: Webb County, Texas, Nov. 19, 2026.
